newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MERGED BELGIAN BANKS TO COMBINE DEALING OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: MERGED BELGIAN BANKS TO COMBINE DEALING OPERATIONS.

text.p: Belgian banks, falling over themselves to merge, are pursuing very different strategies except in one area: dealing rooms.

Cera Bank, which acquired control of Bank Indosuez Belgium last month, has already said it plans to combine its dealing operations. "Dealing room activities will be centralised for certain," a spokesman for the bank said.
It is likely the Bacob/Arco group, which plans to take control of Bank Paribas Belgium and Bank Paribas Nederland later this year, will follow suit, sources said.

"All the big ideas are down on paper. Now only the decisions have to be taken and the practicalities worked out," one source said. One dealing room -- under overall management of Paribas Belgium -- was highly likely.

The greatest impact is likely to be felt in Belgium's debt market, presently dominated by 15 primary dealers, who have preferential rights in auctions of new paper on condition they make a secondary market in it. The mergers seem set to cut the number of primary dealers to 13, possibly by the end of 1997.

Cera Bank has said it will give up one of the two primary dealerships it now has following the acquisition of Indosuez, since renamed Cera Investment Bank. Cera Investment Bank will take the lead in the new dealing operation.
Cera presently has around 30 traders based in Leuven, the same as at Cera Investment Bank in Brussels.
Bank Paribas Belgium and Bacob both have dealing rooms in Brussels with around 75 workstations.
A Paribas/Bacob official said it was likely it will also give up one of its primary dealerships and split the remaining activity -- for OLOs and Treasury bills -- between each bank.
Bank Paribas Belgium, which will be renamed later this year, and Bacob are likely, even if they combine their dealing rooms on one site, to keep separate identities to the outside world, he said.
What is not clear is what will happen to the banks' stock brokerage units -- Ghent-based Nedee & Co for Cera and Antwerp-based Smeets, Verbaet for Bacob/Arco.
"Nedee will be a larger entity, remaining apart from the investment bank but will be the equity house for the group," a Nedee spokeswoman said.
What was not clear was whether Nedee's main trading operation would move to Brussels, or whether Cera Bank equity analysts, presently based in Leuven, would join Nedee.

A Bacob/Paribas source said all options were still open on the future of Smeets. Paribas Belgium also has an equities team and it was not decided if the two would remain separate or be merged, he said.
